2027-01-22.title: Friday of the Second Week in Ordinary Time
readings: I will put my laws in their minds and write them on their hearts
He appointed twelve to be with him and to be sent out
2027-01-22.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 2 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. Week of Prayer for Christian Unity (18–25 January). Optional memorial: St Vincent, deacon and martyr.
2027-01-22.verse: And he appointed twelve, whom he also named apostles, to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message, and to have authority to cast out demons.
theo: Hebrews quotes Jeremiah's great promise of a new covenant: “I will put my laws in their minds, and write them on their hearts, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people… For I will be merciful toward their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more.” The old covenant was written on stone; the new is written by the Spirit on hearts. Christ is its mediator, and forgiveness is its foundation.

Mark shows Jesus forming the people of this new covenant. He goes up the mountain, as Moses did at Sinai, and “called to him those whom he wanted”. He appoints twelve, like the twelve tribes of Israel, for two purposes: “to be with him, and to be sent out”. First friendship, then mission. The list includes fishermen, a tax collector, a zealot and Judas who betrayed him: Jesus calls ordinary, mixed and imperfect people. Every Christian vocation has the same two movements: being with Jesus in prayer, and being sent by him to others.
outline: Ask: why did Jesus choose twelve?
Point 1 · A new covenant on hearts
“To be with him, and to be sent out.”
live: Give fifteen quiet minutes to Jesus today.
Do one act of witness or service in his name today.
2027-01-22.prayer: Lord Jesus, mediator of the new covenant, you called the Twelve to be with you and to be sent out. Write your law on my heart, keep me close to you, and send me to bring your mercy to others. Amen.
altar: At the altar we hear the words: “the new and eternal covenant.” Then the Mass ends: “Go forth.” With him, then sent.

quick: In the new covenant God writes his law on our hearts.
Jesus calls the Twelve to be with him.
He sends them out to proclaim and heal.
2027-01-22.action: Give fifteen quiet minutes to Jesus today, then do one act of service in his name.
2027-01-22.question: Do I spend time with Jesus before I try to work for him?

family.explain: Jesus went up a mountain and chose twelve friends. First they stayed with him, then he sent them to tell everyone about God.
family.intention: We pray for bishops, the successors of the apostles.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we spend time with Jesus this week?”

illus: The Missionaries of Charity of St Teresa of Kolkata spend an hour in adoration every day before going to the poor. A visitor in Kolkata once asked if that was not wasted time with so much work waiting. A sister answered: without the hour with him, we would have nothing to give them.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call us to be with you and to be sent out. Write your law on our hearts as we gather. Amen.
share: I will write them on their hearts (Hebrews 8:10). Is God's law written on my heart or only on paper?
He called to him those whom he wanted (Mark 3:13). How has Jesus called me?
To be with him, and to be sent out (Mark 3:14). Which do I neglect: being with him, or being sent?
interc: For bishops, successors of the apostles.
For new vocations to serve the Church.
For Christian unity, that the Twelve's faith may unite us.
For our group, that we may pray and serve.
pm.close: Father, in your Son you made a new covenant. Keep us close to him and send us out with his mercy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews recalls God's promise through Jeremiah: I will put my laws in their minds, and write them on their hearts, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people (Hebrews 8:10). The new covenant is written not on stone but on hearts, and it rests on forgiveness: I will remember their sins no more.
In the Gospel Jesus goes up the mountain, like Moses at Sinai, and calls to him those whom he wanted. He appoints twelve, a new Israel.
Why does he call them? To be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message (Mark 3:14). First friendship, then mission. The order matters.
The list is surprising: fishermen, a tax collector, a zealot, even Judas. Jesus calls ordinary, imperfect people. He calls you too: first to be with him in prayer, then to go out in his name. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus chose twelve friends. First they stayed with him, then he sent them to help people. Spend time with Jesus, then go and be kind!

intro: Theme: “To be with him, and to be sent out.”
The new covenant written on hearts; the Twelve called and sent.

q: No longer shall they teach one another, or say to each other, “Know the LORD,” for they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest, says the LORD; for I will forgive their iniquity, and remember their sin no more.

This is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their minds, and write them on their hearts, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
points.apply: Memorise one commandment of love this week.

q: And Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD. He rose early in the morning, and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, and set up twelve pillars, corresponding to the twelve tribes of Israel.
And he appointed twelve, whom he also named apostles, to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message, and to have authority to cast out demons.
points.apply: Give Jesus fifteen quiet minutes today.

q: Steadfast love and faithfulness will meet; righteousness and peace will kiss each other.
For I will be merciful toward their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more.”
points.apply: Show mercy to someone who wronged you.

concl: First with him, then sent by him.
The new covenant is mercy written on hearts.
